result: Built a separate 8 GiB Pi 4B raw-image candidate with the current desktop payload, 512 MiB FAT32 firmware/boot partition, and a RedSea data partition with /Home, /Tmp, and two protected source banks. Ordinary RedSea supports bounded FileWrite create/replace, regular-file FileDel, DirMake, empty-directory deletion, and recursive DelTree. Image-builder checks and the disposable stock-RedSea delete/reuse/cold-persistence probe passed. No physical microSD was written.

boot.contents: Raspberry Pi UEFI firmware files and ZealOS boot payload

zealos_data.contents: Full-size RedSea volume with /Home and /Tmp, followed by two 32 MiB append-only source banks

checks: make pi-image completed successfully for this candidate. The builder verified MBR extents, FAT32 boot-sector structure, required firmware and payload read-back, RedSea geometry/root/Home/Tmp/bitmap, and both source-bank headers.
scripts/check-pi-desktop-image.py passed native/recovery ELF identity, load bounds/relocations, two-entry boot chain, and source-module validation.

scripts/check-compat.py --probe-stock-redsea-write passed bounded file create/read/replace/delete, allocation reuse, refusal to directly delete a nonempty directory, empty-directory deletion/recreation, recursive nested DelTree, nested file creation, and all cold-reboot persistence checks with zstatus failed=0.
The RedSea probe used disposable UTM VirtIO storage. It validates filesystem behavior over the generic block layer, not physical Pi SDHCI behavior.
known_scope: Host-built raw image only; it is not the current UTM ISO or a Pi USB-CD installer.
The Pi guest must explicitly run psdopen before ordinary SD writes/deletes; the binding is not restored automatically after reboot.
Physical SD-controller writes, card read-back, cold-boot persistence, and preservation of the FAT boot partition remain unverified.
Rename, automatic directory growth, general writable USB storage, and a Pi-bootable USB installer are not included.
This candidate includes uncommitted source and documentation changes.
